requirement: Enrich an orders DataFrame with customer attributes, guaranteeing each order appears exactly once, duplicate customer keys are rejected, and orders pointing at unknown customers are reported.
skeleton: An UnmatchedOrdersError carrying order ids and attach_customers doing a left many_to_one merge with an indicator, collecting left_only order ids into a sorted error, and dropping the indicator column.
caption: Joining an orders table to a customers table with pandas so bad keys fail loudly. UnmatchedOrdersError is a ValueError subclass holding the offending order_ids. attach_customers(orders, customers) calls orders.merge on customer_id with how left, validate many_to_one so duplicate customer keys raise pandas.errors.MergeError instead of multiplying rows, and indicator True. Rows whose _merge value is left_only are orders without a customer; if any exist their order_id values are converted to int, sorted, and raised in UnmatchedOrdersError. Otherwise the helper _merge column is dropped, and the result keeps every order once in its original order with the customer columns appended. The fixture asserts that four orders keep their order and gain names with columns order_id, customer_id, total, name, that unused customers add no rows, that a duplicated customer key raises MergeError, and that orders for customers 9 and 8 raise UnmatchedOrdersError with order ids 3 and 7.

plan.intent: Build a reporting table from normalized exports
constraints: The merge is a left join on customer_id
validate many_to_one raises MergeError on duplicate customers
Unmatched orders raise UnmatchedOrdersError with sorted ids
Each order appears once in its original order

rationale.teaches: Use merge validate to assert key cardinality and indicator to audit unmatched rows instead of trusting the join.
rationale.why: Duplicate dimension keys silently multiply fact rows, inner joins drop orders without warning, and outer joins invent empty orders.

ops.docstring: Join orders to customers with a validated, audited pandas merge.

candidates.why_wrong: Duplicate customer keys silently duplicate the matching orders.
An inner join silently drops orders whose customer is missing.
The helper _merge indicator column leaks into the result.
An outer join adds rows for customers without orders and reorders rows.
one_to_one validation rejects customers who placed several orders.
